# Release notes: your draft, then mine

Each pair is the first release note description on a PR and the final one after my revisions.

## lak-outlet-ts-link-row.toml

Draft:

> In the Lake (LAK) Package, a time series assigned to an OUTLETS block value (INVERT, WIDTH, ROUGH or SLOPE) was linked under an incorrect row number: an undefined value when the outlet's OUTLETS row exceeded NLAKES, and otherwise a lake number. Simulated outlet values and results were not affected, but the row number reported for the outlet's time-series updates in the listing file (with PRINT\_INPUT) could be wrong, and a large number of outlets relative to lakes could cause an invalid memory read. Outlet time series are now linked under their OUTLETS row.

Mine:

> In the Lake (LAK) Package, a time series assigned to an OUTLETS value was linked to the wrong row: the lake number from the same PACKAGEDATA row or, for OUTLETS rows past NLAKES, a value read out of bounds, which could crash. Simulated values were unaffected, but with PRINT\_INPUT the simulation listing file could name the wrong outlet. Outlet time series are now linked by outlet number.

## gnc-numgnc-check.toml

Draft:

> The GNC package didn't check the number of rows in the GNCDATA block against NUMGNC. With too few rows it read out of bounds, and with too many it ignored the extra rows, which changed results. Either is now an error. A GNCDATA block with no END line at the end of the file, which was previously accepted, is now also an error.

Mine:

> The ghost-node correction (GNC) package now stops with an error if the number of rows in the GNCDATA block does not match NUMGNC. Previously, too few rows could cause a crash or incorrect results, and rows beyond NUMGNC were ignored, so those corrections were not applied. The GNCDATA block must now also end with an END GNCDATA line, which could previously be left out at the end of the file.

## obs-boundname-check.toml

Draft:

> An observation that named a boundary in a package without the BOUNDNAMES option read out of bounds. For a list-based package there was no error, and the observation wrote the no-data value. This is now an error.

Mine:

> An observation that identifies its boundary by name now stops the simulation with an error if the package does not specify the BOUNDNAMES option. Previously the simulation ran, but the observation output contained incorrect values. In the CSUB and UZF packages, an observation whose name matches no boundary is also now an error, even with BOUNDNAMES. Simulated heads and flows were not affected.

## spc-maxbound-check.toml

Draft:

> For SPC6 input, MAXBOUND was only checked against the flow package's number of boundaries in stress periods with an SPC6 PERIOD block or an active time series, and when flows came from a budget file the check used the previous stress period's number of boundaries. A flow package with more boundaries than MAXBOUND could then read invalid concentrations or temperatures without an error. The check now runs every time step.

Mine:

> In GWT and GWE models, a flow package with more boundaries than MAXBOUND in its SPC6 input could go undetected and produce incorrect concentrations or temperatures. This could happen when the number of boundaries increased in a stress period with no SPC6 PERIOD block, or when the transport model was coupled to a separate flow simulation through the Flow Model Interface (FMI) package. The simulation now stops with an error in either of these cases.

## fmi-ats-retry.toml

Draft:

> With adaptive time stepping (ATS), a GWT or GWE model reading flows and heads from file through the Flow Model Interface (FMI) package could stop with an error when a time step failed to converge and was retried. The retry read the next records from the budget and head files instead of reusing the ones already read for that time step. This happened when the first time step of the simulation was retried, and the error reported that the time discretization in the budget file did not match the model's, or that the budget file could not be read. The retried time step now reuses the flows and heads already read.

Mine:

> A GWT, GWE or PRT model using adaptive time stepping and coupled to a flow model through a Flow Model Interface (FMI) package would stop with an error if the first time step of the simulation was retried. Instead of reusing the flows and heads already read for that time step, the retry attempted to read the next records from the budget and head files. The retried time step now reuses the flows and heads already read. Retries of later time steps were not affected.

## mvr-duplicate-packages.toml

Draft:

> The Water Mover (MVR) Package accepted a package listed more than once in the PACKAGES block. The duplicate was counted again in the mover budget written to the listing file, which overstated the package's totals, and it added empty terms with the same names to the budget file. MODFLOW 6 now terminates with an error when a package is listed more than once in the PACKAGES block of a model or exchange mover. Packages with the same name in different models are still allowed in an exchange mover.

Mine:

> The Water Mover (MVR) Package allowed a package to be listed more than once in the PACKAGES block. The duplicate package was double-counted in the mover budget written to the listing file, which overstated the package's totals, and produced empty terms with the same names in the budget file. The program now terminates with an error when a package is listed more than once in the PACKAGES block of a model or exchange mover. Packages with the same name in different models are still allowed in an exchange mover.

## apt-obs-id-check.toml

Draft:

> Advanced transport and energy package observations (LKT, SFT, MWT, UZT, LKE, SFE, MWE and UZE) now stop the simulation with an error when they give a feature number of 0. Previously some of these observations ran and reported a value read from outside the package's arrays. An observation of a feature's aquifer connections (the LKT, SFT, MWT, UZT, LKE, SFE, MWE and UZE types, and the TO-MVR type in LKT and LKE) on a feature with no such connections also no longer reads an uninitialized index. Simulated concentrations, temperatures and flows were not affected.

Mine:

> Observations in the advanced transport and energy packages (LKT, SFT, MWT, UZT, LKE, SFE, MWE and UZE) now stop the simulation with an error when a feature number is 0. Previously such an observation could be accepted and report a meaningless value. An observation of a feature's connections to the aquifer (types LKT, SFT, MWT, UZT, LKE, SFE, MWE and UZE, and TO-MVR in LKT and LKE) on a feature with no such connections is now also an error. Previously its result was unpredictable. Simulated concentrations, temperatures and flows were not affected.

## lak-nlakeconn-zero.toml

Draft:

> In the Lake (LAK) Package, a lake with NLAKECONN equal to zero in the PACKAGEDATA block now stops the simulation with an error. The input instructions have always required NLAKECONN to be greater than zero, but zero was accepted unless the IMPLICIT option was used. A lake with no connections has no bottom elevation, so its results were not meaningful: a lake with CONSTANT status was given a stage of 1e20, and one with ACTIVE status could fail to converge. Such a lake could also cause the simulation to crash, or cause the input for another lake to be misread.

Mine:

> In the Lake (LAK) Package, a lake with NLAKECONN equal to zero in the PACKAGEDATA block now stops the simulation with an error. The input instructions have always required NLAKECONN to be greater than zero, but zero was accepted unless the IMPLICIT option was used. A lake with no connections has no bottom elevation, so its results were not meaningful: a lake with CONSTANT status was given a stage of 1e20, and one with ACTIVE status could fail to converge. Such a lake could also cause the simulation to crash, or cause the input for another lake to be misread. Models with such a lake, even an INACTIVE one, must now remove it or give it a connection.

## ats-retry-end-of-simulation.toml

Draft:

> When an adaptive time step (ATS) in the last stress period would have ended the simulation but failed to converge, the simulation ended after the retried, shorter time step instead of continuing to the end of the period. The simulation now continues to the end of the last stress period.

Mine:

> With adaptive time stepping (ATS), a simulation could end before the end of the last stress period and still report normal termination. This happened when the final time step failed to converge and was retried with a shorter time step: the simulation stopped after the first shorter step that converged. This could have multiple consequences. PRT particles were terminated at that (incorrect) time, or with the EXTEND\_TRACKING option were tracked onward using the flows from that shorter step instead of the flows for the rest of the period. Through the BMI, update\_until returned at the incorrect time as well. Simulations using ATS now run to the end of the last stress period.

## prt-period-blocks-above-nper.toml

Draft:

> In the Particle Release Point (PRP) Package, a file with no release times, no release time frequency, and only PERIOD blocks numbered above NPER has released particles at time zero since version 6.6.3, as if it had no PERIOD blocks. It now releases nothing, as in earlier versions. PRP now also writes a warning when the input configures releases but none will happen, naming the cause: all PERIOD blocks are numbered above NPER, or all release times are negative or fall after the end of the simulation.

Mine:

> If no release times, release time frequency, or PERIOD blocks are given, the Particle Release Point (PRP) Package is intended to default to releasing one particle from each release point at the start of the simulation. Previously, a package with no release times or release time frequency, whose PERIOD blocks were all numbered above NPER (for example after NPER was reduced to temporarily shorten a simulation under development), still applied the default release. Such a package will now release no particles. PRP will now also write a warning when release times or PERIOD blocks are present but no particles will be released, stating the reason. This happens when no PERIOD block is numbered within NPER and no release time falls within the simulation (all release times are negative or, without EXTEND\_TRACKING, beyond the end of the simulation's time discretization).
